the starburst wind is the main agent responsible for the entrainment of dust in M 82, that the starburst disk is responsible for most of the far-IR emission, and that tidal interactions have stripped most of the dust from M 82's disk and are responsible for the dust seen in the halo.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the far-infrared SPIRE maps show that M 82 has a complex distribution of cool dust, with the starburst and disk accounting for only about one third of it.

the far-infrared properties of the wind and halo are not consistent with a single origin, but are rather the product of a combination of processes, with the starburst superwind being the dominant one.
M 82 is not only an excellent example of a starburst galaxy, but also a unique example of the interaction of a starburst with its environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the starburst wind is the dominant contributor to the far-infrared flux in the central 1 kpc, but that the extraplanary emission is dominated by dust entrained in the tidal streams, which are also the source of the bulk of the dust in the halo.
the starburst wind is not the main agent of dust removal from the disk of M82.
the SPIRE maps show that the starburst wind is not as powerful as previously believed, and the bulk of the extraplaran emission arises from the tidal debris of the M 82-M 81 interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the starburst wind is not a significant contributor to the extraplanetary mass distribution.
the far infrared emission from cool dust is an important tracer of extraplanar and tidal material, as well as the starburst wind itself.
a significant fraction of the interstellar medium of M 82 has been removed by the interaction with M 81 and the surrounding intergalactic medium, and is now found outside the starburst region.
